title: Travel Tips for Korea
subtitle: Essential tips for your Korea adventure

items.language: Download Papago or Google Translate for language support.
items.transportation: Get a T-money card for convenient public transport.
items.cash: Many places don't accept foreign cards - carry cash.
items.tipping: Tipping is not customary in Korea.
items.wifi: Free WiFi is widely available in cafes and public areas.

common.tmoney: T-money cards work on buses, subways, and taxis. Get one at any convenience store.
common.cash: Many local shops and traditional markets only accept cash - carry Korean won.
common.operatingHours: Most shops and attractions open at 10-11 AM. Plan morning activities accordingly.

seoul.rushHour: Avoid rush hour (8-9 AM, 6-7 PM) on subway lines 2 and 9 - they get extremely crowded.
seoul.stairsDistance: Seoul involves lots of walking and stairs. Wear comfortable shoes and pace yourself.

busan.coastalWind: Coastal areas can be windy even on warm days. Bring a light jacket for Haeundae Beach.
busan.hills: Many attractions like Gamcheon Village are on steep hills. Plan for extra walking time.

jeju.carRental: Public transport on Jeju is limited. Renting a car is highly recommended for flexibility.
jeju.weatherChange: Jeju weather changes quickly. Always carry rain gear, especially near Hallasan.

gyeongju.historicSites: Historic sites are spread out. Allow at least 2-3 hours for Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto.
gyeongju.bikeRental: Rent a bike to explore the tombs area - it's flat and bike-friendly with dedicated paths.

gangneung.coffeeStreet: Visit Anmok Coffee Street for scenic ocean views and Korea's famous coffee culture.
gangneung.seafood: Try fresh seafood at Jumunjin Market - it's fresher and cheaper than tourist areas.

other.localTransport: In smaller cities, buses may run less frequently. Check schedules on Kakao Map or Naver Map.
other.translation: Papago (Korean translation app) works better than Google Translate for Korean text.

summer.heatHumidity: Summer is hot and humid (30-35°C). Stay hydrated, use sunscreen, and plan indoor breaks.

winter.iceEarlySunset: Winter is cold and dry. Watch for ice on sidewalks and note that sunset is around 5:30 PM.

rainy.indoorAlternatives: Rainy season (장마) brings heavy rain. Have indoor backup plans like museums or shopping malls.

spring.cherryBlossomCrowds: Cherry blossom spots get very crowded in April. Visit early morning for better photos.

fall.perfectWeather: Fall has perfect weather for outdoor activities. Don't miss the autumn foliage at Namsan or Nami Island.
